prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D geometry of an indoor corner with a window high on the left (1.0–1.5 m away in frames 1–2), a quilted mattress surface below (0.5–1.2 m away), an overhead diagonal metal rod on the right (0.2–1.2 m away), and a cylindrical object with a blue cap hanging on a yellow string about 0.1–0.3 m below the rod and 0.4–0.8 m in front of the camera wearer. No other people are present, while the camera wearer's own hands and folded clothes in the lower foreground are brightest at 0.2–0.5 m (well within arm's reach, roughly 0.2–0.4 m to the left of and below the hanging object) and partially cropped at the bottom frame edge. Across the five frames, the camera pitches downward and approaches the mattress by about 0.4 m, shifting the window out of view above while the overhead rod and hanging cylinder move closer and higher in the right foreground, partially occluding the far mattress corner behind them. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the suspended pole, thin hanging string, and dangling cylinder from the similarly toned mattress background and removes harsh window sunlight glare in frames 2–4. However, it looks unreliable in frame 1 where the bright exterior window glass is rendered as closer than the recessed wall corner, and in frame 4 where overexposed clothing merges smoothly into the mattress surface.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only a few foreground elements across the five-frame sequence: the camera wearer's hands in the bottom-left of frames 3 and 5 (at 0.2–0.4 m, within arm's reach), the diagonal overhead rod on the right in frames 2–4 (at 0.3–1.0 m), and the hanging cylinder below the rod in frames 3–4 (at 0.4–0.6 m, about 0.2 m below the rod and 0.2–0.3 m right of the hands). No other people are in the scene; only the camera wearer's own hands enter from the bottom-left edge facing forward and downward toward the mattress, while the rest of the wearer's body remains out of view behind the camera. Across the sequence, as the camera tilts down and moves closer to the mattress, segmented masks appear and vanish intermittently, capturing the approaching rod in frame 2, both the hands and hanging assembly in frame 3, only the rod and hanging cylinder in frame 4, and only the left hand over dark clothing in frame 5. While the sharp mask contours in frames 3 and 4 help delineate the boundary of the pale hanging cylinder against the bright, sunlit mattress where RGB contrast is washed out, the map is highly unreliable overall. It completely misses the room structure, mattress, and clothing, fails to detect anything in frame 1 or the rod in frame 5, and severely misclassifies the metal rod and hanging cylinder as 'toothbrush' and 'spoon'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the five frames, detecting only a single magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's left/both hands in the bottom-left foreground of frame 3 at roughly 0.3 m from the camera. It provides no spatial information about the surrounding room layout, the mattress at 0.5–1.2 m, the overhead rod on the right, or the hanging cylinder 0.2–0.3 m to the right of the hands, though it confirms that no other people are present or facing the camera wearer. In frame 3, the detected hand skeleton is within immediate arm's reach in front of and below the camera, oriented forward with fingers curled around the white cloth, and partly truncated at the lower frame boundary where the wrists and arms extend out of view. Across frames 1 to 5, as the camera pitches down toward the bed and the wearer's hands reach in and out of the lower-left field of view, the pose estimator fails to track the movement prior to or after frame 3. In frame 3, the magenta keypoints reveal the articulated finger joints of the overlapping hands that are partially washed out by bright sunlight on the white fabric in the RGB image, but the map is unreliable because it completely misses the visible right hand in frame 1 and the outstretched left hand in frame 5, and merges the two closely overlapping hands in frame 3 into a single distorted skeleton.
